questions.question: What is the difference between a class and an object?
options: They are the same thing
A class is a blueprint/template; an object is an actual thing built from that blueprint
An object is a blueprint; a class is a thing built from it
A class stores data; an object stores functions
questions.explanation: A class is the blueprint (like the design for a house), and an object (or instance) is an actual thing created from it (an actual house). One class can create many objects, each with its own data.

questions.question: When does the __init__ method run?
options: Every time any method is called
Automatically when you create a new object from the class
Only when you call it directly with obj.__init__()
Never — it's just documentation
questions.explanation: __init__ runs automatically each time you create an object (e.g. Dog('Rex')). It's the constructor, where you set up the object's starting data. You never call it directly yourself.

questions.question: What does self refer to inside a method?
options: The class itself
The specific object the method is being called on
A global variable
The parent class
questions.explanation: self refers to the particular object the method was called on. When you write rex.bark(), Python passes rex in as self. That's how one method can work on many different objects — self points to a different one each time.

questions.question: In class Dog(Animal):, what does this mean?
options: Dog contains an Animal
Dog inherits from Animal, getting all its attributes and methods
Animal inherits from Dog
Dog and Animal are the same class
questions.explanation: class Dog(Animal) means Dog inherits from Animal. Dog automatically gets all of Animal's methods and attributes, and can add its own or override them. This models an 'is-a' relationship: a Dog is an Animal.

questions.question: Why is inheritance especially important for AI with PyTorch?
options: It makes code run faster
Every neural network you build inherits from nn.Module, getting PyTorch's machinery for free
It removes the need for functions
It is only used for printing models
questions.explanation: In PyTorch you write class MyModel(nn.Module). By inheriting from nn.Module, your model automatically gets parameter tracking, GPU support, saving/loading, and more — you only add the parts specific to your model.

exercises.prompt: Write a class Rectangle with an __init__ that stores width and height, and a method area that returns width times height.
hints: In __init__, store the values with self.width = width and self.height = height.
In area, return self.width * self.height. Don't forget the self. prefix to access the object's data.

exercises.prompt: Write a class Counter with an __init__ that sets self.count to 0, and a method increment that adds 1 to self.count each time it's called.
hints: In increment, write self.count += 1 to add one each call.

exercises.prompt: Create a base class Animal with a method describe that returns the string "I am an animal". Then create a subclass Dog that inherits from Animal and adds a method speak returning "Woof".
hints: Animal.describe should return "I am an animal".
Dog inherits describe automatically via class Dog(Animal). Just add speak returning "Woof".
